title: Streaming and Waivers with FAB and 6 Adds per Week
brief: How should we use our streaming spot, FAB budget and 6 weekly adds to gain games and value in our daily H2H league? It must cover the value of a streaming slot, what to react to early in the season, which categories are easy to stream, and the discovery, optimizing and maximizing phases of the season.
summary: In our league, a streaming slot is worth about a top 100 to 110 player. Keep one roster spot open for streaming instead of spending auction money on a low-upside 12th man, and use the 6 weekly adds steadily. Be patient in weeks one and two and evaluate roles. Churn the end of the roster in midseason, then drop stashes and stream as hard as you can in playoff weeks 19 to 21, which end 2027-03-28.

sections.heading: What a streaming slot is worth

paragraphs.text: The notes agree that one streaming slot is worth about a top 100 player. One note puts it at a top 100 to 110 player. Our draft takes 144 players. So the fringe of your roster competes with a slot that is worth more than most players taken after pick 100.

Auction rule: do not budget for all 12 spots out of your 200 USD. Plan for at most 11 real players and leave one bench spot for streaming. If a low-upside player is ranked around 115, drop him and stream that spot or use it for fliers.

Games played is the reason. Streaming players ranked 170 to 190 for extra games beats holding a 130th-ranked player who sits on your bench. With daily lineups, a stream only helps when his game fills an empty active slot. Check your schedule before each add.

Long-term injured players cost you that streaming production if they hold a normal roster spot. We have 4 IL slots, so put them there. If your IL is full, weigh each injured stash against a slot worth about a 100th-ranked player.

The experts frame the value a little differently. One says a streaming slot equals about the 100th player. Another says the 100th to 110th. A third gives the 115 cutoff for dropping low-upside players. The practical range is the same: anyone you would rank worse than about 110 to 115, with no upside, should give way to streaming.

sections.heading: Using FAB and 6 adds per week

paragraphs.text: Know the rules, because they change player value. Our waivers run daily on a FAB budget, with a limit of 6 acquisitions per week. One note says that with unlimited moves the end of a roster should churn all the time, and with only two moves a week you should still use both. With 6, the same logic says to use your adds, not save them.

The waiver wire matters as much as the draft. Value comes from draft picks that beat their price, streaming, hot pickups who stay hot, and short-term injury replacements. The notes give no FAB bid amounts. Save bigger bids for role changes that will last. Treat short fill-in jobs as cheap streams.

Good streaming profiles from the notes: backup centers who start when the starter sits, and bench players on thin teams during heavy schedule stretches when starters rest. A backup center can also pick up minutes when the starter is in foul trouble, hurt or not scoring. Older players back from major injuries will likely sit back-to-backs early, which opens games for their backups.
Do not hold a backup center for the long term. He is not worth a roster spot until the starter in front of him is out. Add him on the nights or weeks he starts, then cut him.

sections.heading: Which categories are easy to stream

paragraphs.text: Threes are easy to find on waivers. Do not pay up for three-point specialists in the auction. A build with non-shooters loses little in 3PTM, because waivers can cover it.
Steals are one of the most common categories on the wire. They also skew standard 9-cat rankings. So you can pick up steals with streamers and should not pay extra for them at the draft.
Assists are the opposite. They are very hard to find on waivers and the category matters. Get your assists at the draft, then stream for the easy categories.

Turnovers fight streaming. TO is the only negative counting stat in our 9 categories. More games played means more turnovers. If you stream for volume, you will often give up TO. Do not hold back on streaming just to protect it.

sections.heading: Discovery phase: weeks one and two

paragraphs.text: The season has three phases: discovery, optimizing and maximizing. Discovery is the opening stretch after the 2026-10-18 draft. Its goal is to learn which roles are real.

Watch for unexpected minutes, new starters, depth chart changes and players doing more. Coaches do strange things in weeks one and two. Move fast on real role changes, such as a new 28-minute starting job. Do not react to bad shooting nights if role, minutes and usage are unchanged.
Do not stream just to get extra games in week one. Accept losses in weeks one and two so you can keep fliers with longer-term value. Losing week one is fine.

The experts differ on how long to hold fliers. One says to drop a rookie flier if nothing happens in the first two weeks, and maybe pick him up again later. Another says to drop late fliers if things are not working after a few weeks. Both agree you should not hold several inefficient rookie fliers at once. Pick the ones to keep and cut the rest quickly.
Injuries peak early in the season because camp and preseason are short. They fall off by mid-December. Expect the most fill-in streaming chances in October and November.

From about mid-season on, churn the end of your roster and use your 6 weekly adds. Do not drop proven players after a cold stretch. Do not chase hot streaks that will settle back to normal. Every player has games above and below his average.

Value a fill-in starter by his healthy-team role. A bench player who posts numbers in big minutes during an injury should be expected to rank around 150th unless something changes. That is a stream, not a big FAB bid. Do not boost him much for a short injury that may last a few games or none.

If a player who is not a real starter is putting up starter numbers, sell him then, because the numbers will not improve. Trades are frequent in our league. Make those sales before the trade deadline on 2027-03-04.

Maximizing comes near the end of the season and in the playoffs. Drop stashed and injured players and stream as much as you can. Our playoffs are weeks 19, 20 and 21 and end Sunday 2027-03-28. Plan your games and adds around that date, not the April 4 default.

In those weeks, games played is the main edge. Use all 6 adds to fill open daily slots. Look first for backup centers taking over starts and for bench players on thin teams when starters rest. Accept the extra turnovers that come with more games.

Expect a smaller late-season injury spike than usual. One note says there should be fewer fake injuries this year. Do not count on rest days alone to create streamers. Check daily who is actually starting.
